summary.intent: Add --kind flag to memory-loop refresh to focus generation on a specific memory kind (repo_rule, skill_patch, etc.), print the generation threshold under the scope line, and fix TUI threshold changes not persisting to refresh.
summary.outcome: All three features were implemented and committed: TUI threshold now propagates to refresh, threshold prints after scope line, and --kind flag focuses both the LLM prompt and post-generation filtering on the specified memory kind.

repo: TUI settings (GenerationThreshold, GenerationOverrides, InjectionScopes) were saved to memory-loop.json but not loaded before refresh's threshold resolution — required moving loadMemoryLoopState earlier in the refresh flow.
Store rebuild in refresh was dropping InjectionScopes, GenerationThreshold, and GenerationOverrides fields, losing TUI settings across refreshes.

GenerateInput.KindFocus narrows the LLM prompt's kind enum to a single value AND adds a kind-specific directive string; buildGeneratedRecordsDetailed also filters mismatched kinds post-generation as a safety net.
KindFocus and FilteredKindCount are tracked in RefreshHistory in memoryloop.go for observability.
The five valid memory kinds are: repo_rule, workflow_rule, agent_instruction, skill_patch, anti_pattern.

code.finding: LLM prompt uses a JSON schema with 'kind' field — when KindFocus is set, the enum narrows to a single value and a kind-specific directive is appended to the guidelines.
runMemoryLoopRefresh signature extended with a 'kind string' parameter; all test call sites required updating to pass empty string.

workflow: Moving state/threshold resolution above session loading and backfill is purely cosmetic (allows earlier printing) — backfill behavior is unaffected by threshold.
Pre-existing lint issues (goconst 'balanced', maintidx) should be verified against baseline before attributing to changes.
Test call sites for internal functions must be updated when signatures change — grep for all usages before editing.

friction: Assistant accidentally ran `git checkout` during a lint baseline check which reverted the working changes, requiring both edits to be re-applied from scratch.
Duplicate state-loading and threshold-print blocks were left in the file after restructuring and required a separate cleanup edit.
User interrupted mid-edit to redirect from a simpler filter-only approach to a more comprehensive prompt-tailoring approach.
open_items: The --kind flag focuses the LLM but doesn't affect summary backfill or facet computation — no filtering there by design, but worth noting for future kind-scoped workflows.
Pre-existing lint issues (goconst 'balanced', maintidx on large functions) were not fixed as part of this work.
implementation_rationale: KindFocus narrows the LLM prompt's kind enum rather than just post-filtering because a focused prompt produces better signal — the model spends its output budget on the requested kind rather than generating all kinds and discarding most.
Post-generation filter kept as belt-and-suspenders because LLMs don't always follow schema constraints perfectly.
Threshold resolution moved before session loading purely to enable earlier printing; no behavioral change was intended or introduced.
tradeoffs: Prompt tailoring means the LLM generates fewer total candidates when --kind is used, but higher-relevance ones for the target kind vs. generating all kinds and filtering.
The kind-specific directive strings are hardcoded in BuildPrompt rather than driven by a map/config — simpler but requires code changes to add new kinds.
codebase_patterns: Mode, MaxInjected, ActivationPolicy already followed the pattern of TUI state overriding settings.json — GenerationThreshold/GenerationOverrides/InjectionScopes were brought in line with this pattern.
RefreshHistory struct tracks metadata about each refresh run (threshold, kind, counts) for observability.
memoryloop package owns generation types (GenerateInput, GenerationStats, RefreshHistory); CLI command wires flags to those types.
